neighbours.label: 'as to' after a noun of uncertainty or inquiry (doubt / question / speculation / idea as to whether, who, the cause); fires on ' as' and ' to'; other uses of 'as' or 'so as to' do not fire
fire: The letter left no doubt as to who would inherit the farm.
There has been much speculation as to whether the factory will close.
Historians still raise the question as to why the fleet turned back.
The witness gave no clue as to where the money had gone.
The report offers little guidance as to how the funds should be spent.
Investigators remain in the dark as to who started the rumour.
There is some confusion as to whether the rule applies to visitors.
The court expressed no opinion as to whether the contract was valid.
quiet: The letter left no doubt that her niece would inherit the farm.
There has been much talk that the factory will close.
Historians still ask why the fleet turned back.
The witness worked as a clerk where the money had gone.
The report was written so as to show how the funds should be spent.
Investigators remain in the dark, as the rumour spread quickly.
The rule is as strict for visitors as for members.
The court was as silent as the contract was long.

notes: Card: ' to' x18 and ' as' x13 of the top 32, all in 'N as to wh-' with N = doubt, question, idea, speculation; the - pole is other prepositions after the same nouns (uncertainty in, insight of). Probes: 'doubt as to whether' 0.83, 'idea as to the cause' 0.41; 'doubt about whether' 0.19, 'worked as a nurse' 0.00, 'so as to' 0.03, sentence-initial 'As to' 0.15.
